gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Garmin's 'unlimited with solar' rating for the Instinct 3 Solar assumes 3 hours a day outdoors at 50,000 lux. Without that sun the 45 mm model is rated 28 days, against 27 for the Amazfit T-Rex 3, and in multi-band GPS it is rated 24 h against the T-Rex 3's 42 h dual-band.
standout_why: I compared against the cited mobileplustech.com guide (2026-11-01). It gives no battery hours or days and no prices. On solar it says only that it 'adds hours or days per week in sunny conditions'. I asked WebFetch for the cited TechRadar T-Rex 3 Pro review twice, but it returned only the headline, so I can't say what that review lists. Neither readable page puts the brands' battery claims on a common basis or quotes Garmin's 50,000 lux footnote.
decides: ChatGPT ranked the Instinct 3 Solar 'best overall' for 'excellent battery endurance'. Without sun, the 45 mm Instinct 3 Solar matches the cheaper-at-launch T-Rex 3 on smartwatch days (28 vs 27). In multi-band GPS the T-Rex 3 is rated 1.75× longer (42 h vs 24 h; 40 h for the Garmin in sun). So battery alone does not justify the Garmin pick. Its edge holds only for buyers who are outdoors in strong sun every day, or who pay for the 50 mm (34 h, 60 h with sun). Separately, Apple's current model is the Ultra 4 (50 h normal use), not the Ultra 3 that ChatGPT showed. Even so, Apple's battery is rated in hours, while Garmin and Amazfit rate theirs in weeks.
